title: Nobody's Company
lead: Cinder Reach has stopped. Six thousand miners hold the Gate on Shift Row, Director Rennick Vale has hired men with clubs, and Shift Boss Ulla Greaves stands on an ore cart telling the crowd that anyone in a uniform had better pick a side before the dome lights go down.
anyone: Cinder Reach has stopped. Six thousand miners hold the Gate on Shift Row, Director Rennick Vale has hired men with clubs, and Shift Boss Ulla Greaves stands on an ore cart telling the crowd that anyone in a uniform had better pick a side before the dome lights go down.

gm.truth: The grievances are real: cut vent budgets, unpaid wages, ration chits that buy less each week, and a door in Shaft Nine that Rennick Vale ordered shut with fourteen people behind it. Ulla wants to hear him say it. But nobody knows the strange part except Rennick. There's no company. The owners were on Asterion. The holding bank fell with the Concord. For six months Rennick has been running the refinery with no boss and no money, printing ration chits on the office press up on Company Hill and telling everyone the head office is reviewing their demands, because if the skeleton crew at the Stack stops believing there's a company, they walk, and he's the only one who knows what happens at the Tap if they do. The strikebreakers are paid in stolen fuel. The ruthless director with the broken windows is a frightened man forging his own employer's letters. Ulla Greaves is striking against no one. And if the miners learned it, they might discover that the refinery, the fuel and the moon are simply theirs, if they can keep them. Ulla's treasurer, Ness Bray, knows who's really paying for the strike kitchen, and he isn't sharing that with her either.
beats: The Gate. Heat, slag-light, and thousands of tired people who won't say a hard word to you for crossing it, and will only remember. Ulla gives the captain ten honest minutes and a list of demands, counted on her fingers. Her bluntness is a relief after everyone else.

Rennick's office on Company Hill, its windows repaired for the eleventh time, and a very good bottle he doesn't touch. He limps. He offers the same fuel to use the fleet's security against the Gate, and he says everything a villain would say. A careful eye notices the letterhead is still wet. His daughter is down on the picket line with a loudhailer, shouting his name.
The tension breaks: a strikebreaker is badly hurt, or a miner is, and Shift Row starts to move. The captain has about an hour before it's a riot.
The truth comes out, by a hacked ledger, a confession or a printing press with the head office's stamp still inked. Rennick, cornered, says it out loud. Ulla doesn't believe it, and then she does.
What now? Six thousand people, a refinery nobody owns, and the fleet's fuel hanging on who runs it, with the Syndicate, the Hegemony and Rennick's own hired men each very interested in the answer.
routes: Broker it: persuasion and leadership to get Ulla and Rennick to a table, keep Shift Row from exploding and walk them through the truth.
Dig it up: hacking, commerce and awareness to read the refinery's books and see that no money has come in for six months.
Hold the line: intimidation and tactics to stare down the strikebreakers, or to stand between them and the crowd long enough for cooler heads to win.
checks: persuasion:hard to get Ulla Greaves to sit down with Rennick
leadership:hard to stop a crowd of thousands in one speech
hacking:moderate to get into the refinery's accounts
commerce:moderate to see from the ledger that no one has paid for anything since the Fall
intimidation:moderate to make hired men think twice about their pay
tactics:moderate to place the fleet's few security people where it matters
fights: strikebreaker at the Gate if the riot starts. Unpaid men don't fight long, once someone tells them nobody's going to pay them.
outcomes: If the miners take over the refinery with Rennick still alive and working, Cinder Reach becomes a free colony that sells fuel to the fleet at a fair price. It's the best fuel deal in known space, and everyone with a fleet of their own will notice.
If Rennick is thrown to the crowd, Shift Row cheers, and nobody on the moon now knows how the Tap works. That leads to the worst possible start on the next thread.

If the captain keeps the secret and takes Rennick's deal, the fleet gets fuel, the strike is broken, and eventually the miners find out. Ulla Greaves doesn't forget or forgive, and she can reach a long way.
If the Syndicate or the Hegemony learns first, Quill or Corvane turns up with a very reasonable offer to buy a refinery from nobody at all.
gm.rewards: A fair fuel contract if the captain brokers peace, one or two refined_fuel up front, a work_suit, and the friendship of Ulla Greaves, who says what she thinks and keeps her word.
